Beyond the already-noted mock-GPS spoofing, the always-on covert background location tracker is a ready-made stalkerware primitive (install on a partner's/child's phone, it silently tracks and can be observed), and there is no protection against malicious/oversized route injection, notification abuse, or reverse-engineering of the Directions/Places API key.
cases.failure_mode: App is repurposed for covert surveillance (a real safety/abuse vector for an always-tracking, quiet-notification app), or a crafted/huge route or spoofed fix corrupts progress and mis-fires the alarm. No tamper/mock detection in the alarm path, no misuse safeguards.
cases.evidence: No position.isMocked check in the alarm path (consistent with the existing network-positioning LOW). Persistent tracking runs with a quiet/paused-style notification (notification_service.dart), i.e. low-visibility background tracking. No API-key restriction/attestation evidence. Abuse/stalkerware and adversarial-input classes are unconsidered.

cases.scenario: NEW DIMENSION multi-user / shared-device / remote-arming. India-common shared family phones and the realistic need to wake someone else (e.g. arm an alarm for a child or elderly parent riding, or hand the phone over) are unmodeled: there is no profile concept, and only one active journey/alarm state keyed by route with no per-user separation.
cases.failure_mode: On a shared phone, one family member's armed journey collides with another's (and the existing timing-duration key-collision GAP shows same-route state already clobbers), or a rider who wanted to arm on behalf of another person has no mechanism. Multi-user reality silently corrupts single-user assumptions.
cases.evidence: Alarm/route state is single-tenant and keyed without a user dimension (route_session_manager.dart:134-139 makeKey without user; route_queue.dart tracks only activeRouteIndex). No profiles/accounts. This extends the existing 'repeat/identical-route key collision' timing-duration GAP into the multi-user case.

cases.scenario: NEW DIMENSION monetization / commercial lifecycle. If/when the app monetizes (trial, subscription, ads), no thought is given to a subscription lapse or expired trial that fires MID-JOURNEY and could gate the alarm, an interstitial ad or paywall obscuring the wake screen, or offline riders being unable to validate entitlement underground. Currently there is no billing code at all, so the entire commercial-edge dimension is simply absent from the design.
cases.failure_mode: A future entitlement check that fails closed (e.g. subscription expired at 3am, or offline receipt-validation underground) would block the alarm — turning a billing state into a missed stop. A paywall/ad over the full-screen alarm would suppress the wake cue. None of this is guarded against because monetization was never scoped.
cases.evidence: No billing/purchase/subscription SDK in lib (grep for in_app_purchase/BillingClient/StoreKit/entitlement empty). Because it is unbuilt, there is no fail-open guarantee that alarm firing is independent of any future entitlement/ads layer — a design hole to lock down before monetizing.

cases.scenario: First-time rider installs on a budget phone (Redmi/Realme, common in India), arms a metro alarm, locks the screen and dozes. Aggressive OS battery optimization (default ON for new apps) freezes/kills the flutter_background_service after some minutes of Doze.
cases.failure_mode: The foreground tracking service is suspended, GPS/EKF stops updating, and the alarm never fires. Rider sleeps past the stop. This is the exact 'fire late = product death' outcome.
cases.evidence: There is NO battery-optimization handling anywhere. Manifest (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml) does not declare REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS; grep for isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations/ignoreBatteryOptimizations across lib/ returns nothing. pubspec has battery_plus (reads battery level only) and android_intent_plus but no disable-battery-optimization flow. PermissionService (lib/services/permission_service.dart) requests only location, notification, activityRecognition. Service runs as isForegroundMode:true (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:210) which is necessary but insufficient against OEM Doze without whitelisting.

cases.scenario: Rider on Xiaomi MIUI / Oppo/Realme ColorOS / Vivo FuntouchOS (the dominant Indian budget stack) where the OEM aggressively kills backgrounded apps and requires a manual 'Autostart' + 'No battery restrictions' toggle buried in a vendor-specific settings screen.
cases.failure_mode: Even with Android-standard permissions granted, the vendor kills the service; the alarm silently never fires. The rider has no idea a hidden OEM toggle exists.
cases.evidence: grep for xiaomi|oppo|vivo|oem|autostart|manufacturer across lib/ returns nothing. No onboarding screen exists (grep onboard|tutorial|walkthrough|firstRun|hasSeen returns nothing). SplashScreen (lib/screens/splash_screen.dart) goes straight to init+home with no education. No per-OEM deep-link or guidance is ever presented.

cases.scenario: Android 11+ rider grants foreground location at the 'Wake Me' prompt. The app then immediately calls Permission.locationAlways.request() for 'Allow all the time', which on Android 11+ CANNOT be granted inline — the OS either returns while-in-use silently or requires a manual trip to app Settings.
cases.failure_mode: _requestBackgroundLocation returns false, requestEssentialPermissions returns false, canProceed is false, and _onWakeMePressed just resets the loading spinner. The trip never starts and, if the rider tapped through, tracking runs only 'while in use' — dies the moment the screen locks. No Settings guidance is offered for background location.
cases.evidence: lib/services/permission_service.dart _requestBackgroundLocation() shows a rationale then calls Permission.locationAlways.request() and returns status.isGranted — it never checks isPermanentlyDenied and has NO _showSettingsDialog path (unlike location/notification). homescreen.dart:481-499: on failure the else branch only does setState(_isLoading=false) with the comment 'The service already showed the user a dialog' — which is false for the background-location decline path.

cases.scenario: Android 14+ rider (increasingly common on newer budget phones) installs fresh. The wake alarm relies on a full-screen intent to light up the lockscreen. On Android 14+, USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is granted by default only to apps in the alarm/calling category; a generic app must be granted 'full-screen notifications' special access.
cases.failure_mode: The full-screen alarm UI is demoted to a normal notification behind the lockscreen. On a silenced/dozing phone the rider is not forcefully woken; the alarm effectively under-fires. There is no runtime check nor education to request this special access.
cases.evidence: Manifest declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT and notification_service.dart:729 sets fullScreenIntent:true ('critical for lockscreen appearance'), but grep for canUseFullScreenIntent|requestFullScreenIntentPermission returns nothing. No code queries or requests the Android 14+ special access.

cases.scenario: Cold first launch: main.dart fires _checkNotificationPermission() from initState, showing the bare Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS system prompt before the user has seen any explanation of what the app does. Reflexively the user taps 'Deny'.
cases.failure_mode: POST_NOTIFICATIONS becomes denied (and after a second denial, permanently denied). Since the wake-up is delivered via a notification channel, a permanent denial later dead-ends: the only remedy PermissionService offers is a Settings dialog the sleepy rider must navigate. Poor priming turns a recoverable prompt into a permanent block.
cases.evidence: lib/main.dart:78-83 _checkNotificationPermission() calls Permission.notification.request() with no rationale/priming, at app-launch, before onboarding. PermissionService._requestNotificationPermission (permission_service.dart) does handle the permanent-denial case with _showSettingsDialog, so it is not a total GAP — but the un-primed early prompt makes permanent denial likely.

cases.scenario: At the 'Wake Me' rationale/background dialog the (hurried, already-boarding) rider taps 'Not Now' or 'Cancel' instead of Continue.
cases.failure_mode: The flow returns false with no follow-up. The user presses Wake Me, dismisses the dialog, and the button silently resets to idle with nothing happening and no error toast — the rider reasonably assumes the alarm is armed when it is not.
cases.evidence: permission_service.dart _showRationaleDialog returns false on 'Not Now'; the caller returns false. homescreen.dart _onWakeMePressed else branch only does setState(() => _isLoading = false) — no _showErrorDialog, relying on the incorrect assumption that 'the service already showed the user a dialog'. When the rider declined the rationale, no dialog was shown afterward.

cases.scenario: All permissions are demanded at the moment of arming the trip (Wake Me press) rather than during a calm onboarding — so the rider is already inside the moving metro/bus, on flaky connectivity, when told to leave the app and go to system Settings to grant 'Allow all the time'.
cases.failure_mode: The rider must background the app to fix Settings exactly as the journey begins; many abandon and start the trip with while-in-use location, which dies at screen lock. Worst-possible timing for a multi-step Settings trip.
cases.evidence: Permissions are requested lazily inside _onWakeMePressed (homescreen.dart:481-483), not at install/onboarding. No pre-trip readiness screen exists. The background-location grant inherently requires a Settings excursion on Android 11+ (see permission_service.dart _requestBackgroundLocation), which is triggered at trip-start.

cases.scenario: Infrequent rider uses WakePoint only for occasional travel. Android's 'auto-reset permissions for unused apps' (default) revokes location after a few months of non-use; the rider re-arms for a big journey.
cases.failure_mode: PermissionService re-checks on each Wake Me press (good), but a revoked-to-permanently-denied background location dead-ends because _requestBackgroundLocation has no Settings path, silently blocking the trip; foreground-only revocation is recoverable but background is not guided.
cases.evidence: PermissionService.requestEssentialPermissions is invoked each Wake Me press (homescreen.dart:481), so foreground location and notification re-prompt with their _showSettingsDialog fallbacks. But _requestBackgroundLocation (permission_service.dart) still lacks any isPermanentlyDenied/_showSettingsDialog branch, so an auto-reset that lands background location in permanent-deny cannot be remediated in-app.

cases.scenario: Rider denies (or the un-guided request silently fails for) ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION / HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS, which the EKF dead-reckoning relies on to keep tracking through underground metro tunnels.
cases.failure_mode: When the train enters a tunnel and GPS drops, the EKF has degraded/no IMU input, so dead-reckoning over the known route underperforms — precisely the tunnel scenario the product exists to solve. The denial is swallowed with no user feedback.
cases.evidence: permission_service.dart _requestActivityRecognitionPermission() calls request() and ignores the result entirely (comment: 'less critical, so we can just request it'), returning void; requestEssentialPermissions treats it as non-critical. Manifest declares ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION and HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS but nothing educates or verifies. (Impact is latent since the task notes EKF is not yet wired into production alarm logic, but the permission gap is baked in.)

cases.scenario: Rider grants everything correctly on the very first journey, but there is no post-setup confirmation that tracking will actually survive a locked, dozing screen (no readiness check combining background-location + battery-whitelist + notification + full-screen-intent status).
cases.failure_mode: The rider gets no signal distinguishing 'armed and will really work' from 'armed but will silently die', so the first real overnight trip is the test — and if any OEM/battery condition is off, they discover it by missing the stop.
cases.evidence: No aggregated readiness/health screen exists; grep for onboard|tutorial|firstRun|hasSeen returns nothing and SplashScreen (splash_screen.dart) only restores session state. PermissionService returns a single bool with no per-condition surfacing of battery-optimization or full-screen-intent status (neither of which it even checks).

dimension: platform-parity/iOS — background execution & alarm delivery (the entire tracking/alarm stack is Android-designed; iOS suspends the app on screen-lock, so the position stream, EKF, and live alarm never run)

cases.scenario: Core use case: an iOS rider sets a wake-up alarm, locks the phone, and falls asleep on the train. iOS suspends the Flutter app within seconds of screen-lock/backgrounding.
cases.failure_mode: The suspended app produces zero GPS updates, so the position-stream loop that drives ALL alarm evaluation never runs. The rider sails past their stop and is never woken. Silent, total failure for every iOS rider on the primary journey.
cases.evidence: ios/Runner/Info.plist declares NO <key>UIBackgroundModes</key> at all (no 'location', 'audio', or 'processing'). trackingservice.dart:604-607 onIosBackground() is a no-op that just returns true. The alarm is only ever evaluated inside LocationManager().positionStream.listen(...) in location_stream_handler.dart:209 — when iOS suspends the app that stream stops and the loop dies. There is no OS mechanism keeping the app alive.

cases.scenario: Even a rider whose ETA is roughly known in advance (metro N-minutes-before mode) locks the phone; one might expect a pre-scheduled fallback notification to fire at the target time while suspended.
cases.failure_mode: There is no pre-scheduled alarm. All alarms are shown live at the moment of evaluation, so while the app is suspended nothing is queued in iOS's notification scheduler to fire. No wake-up.
cases.evidence: notification_service.dart uses _notificationsPlugin.show() everywhere (lines 818, 906, 968, 1100, 1202) and never zonedSchedule/periodicallyShow. Alarm origin is triggerAlarm invoked from the live loop (alarm_controller.dart:281, 449, 521, 694, 788). Nothing is scheduled with iOS ahead of time, so suspension = no delivery.

cases.scenario: iOS rider enters a metro tunnel (the exact case the EKF dead-reckoning was built for) with the phone locked. GPS is lost and the app is already suspended.
cases.failure_mode: The EKF/sensor-fusion fallback that is supposed to dead-reckon over the known route also never runs, because it too lives in the suspended background isolate and is fed by the same halted position stream. Motion sensor delivery also stops. The one feature meant to save tunnel riders is doubly dead on iOS.
cases.evidence: SensorFusionManager/EKF is driven from the same background isolate (trackingservice.dart:617 _sensorFusionManager, location_stream_handler.dart:585 ekfStateStream) which iOS suspends. No UIBackgroundModes 'location' or 'processing' in Info.plist means neither Core Location nor a background task keeps the isolate scheduled. NSMotionUsageDescription exists but motion updates are not delivered to a suspended app.

cases.scenario: The app requests 'Always' location permission on iOS, the rider grants it, and reasonably believes background tracking now works.
cases.failure_mode: Granting Always-location does nothing without the background-location capability. iOS still stops delivering updates to the suspended app, so the rider gets a false sense of safety, relies on the alarm, and misses the stop. This is worse than an outright denial because it hides the failure.
cases.evidence: permission_service.dart:60-70 requests Permission.locationAlways and Info.plist has NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription, so the user is prompted for Always. But there is NO AppleSettings/allowBackgroundLocationUpdates anywhere (grep of lib/ returns none — location_manager.dart:45 uses generic LocationSettings) and no UIBackgroundModes 'location'. Background delivery therefore never happens despite the granted permission.

cases.scenario: Suppose a notification somehow fires on iOS while the rider is asleep with a Sleep Focus / Do Not Disturb enabled (typical for someone napping) and the phone on silent.
cases.failure_mode: The delivered notification is silent and non-urgent: it does not bypass Focus/DND, plays no sound, and the loud alarm audio can't start because it requires the app to be running. The rider sleeps through a soundless banner.
cases.evidence: notification_service.dart:772-774 DarwinNotificationDetails sets presentSound: false and never sets interruptionLevel critical/timeSensitive; DarwinInitializationSettings() at line 563-564 requests no critical-alert permission and there is no ios/*.entitlements file granting com.apple.developer.usernotifications.critical-alerts. The loud sound comes from AlarmPlayer (alarm_player.dart:20 AVAudioSessionCategory.playback) which needs the app alive and has no UIBackgroundModes 'audio' to start playback while backgrounded.

cases.scenario: The heartbeat 'foreground process was killed' safety net is expected to detect loss of tracking on iOS the way it does for Android app-swipe.
cases.failure_mode: On iOS the foreground and the background isolate are suspended together, so the heartbeat monitor cannot detect anything (it too is frozen), and even if it did, its recovery action is another show() notification that cannot be delivered while suspended. The one watchdog is inoperative on iOS.
cases.evidence: heartbeat_monitor.dart runs on Timer.periodic inside the background isolate (isEnabled gated on _isBackgroundIsolate, trackingservice.dart:625-627) which iOS pauses; its timeout handler calls NotificationService().showTrackingPaused() (heartbeat_monitor.dart) via show(), unavailable while suspended. The whole design comment says it detects the foreground being 'swiped away/killed' — an Android model that doesn't map to iOS suspension.

cases.scenario: iOS rider on a cheap/older phone in Low Power Mode (common in India-first market, and common for someone who dozed off with a low battery) backgrounds the app.
cases.failure_mode: Low Power Mode makes iOS even more aggressive about suspending and denying background execution and location. With no significant-location-change or CLVisit monitoring registered as a coarse fallback, there is literally no code path that can wake the app to re-evaluate the alarm.
cases.evidence: No significant-location-change / CLVisit / BGTaskScheduler usage anywhere (grep of location_stream_handler.dart and lib/ finds none). The service is configured autoStart:false (trackingservice.dart:220) and start-on-demand only, so once suspended nothing re-launches it.

cases.scenario: iOS rider, realizing they've been asleep, re-opens the app near/at their stop hoping the recovery/snapshot logic catches them up.
cases.failure_mode: Snapshot restore only runs when the user manually foregrounds the app; by then the app may resume past the target stop with a stale last-known position, and there was no alarm during the gap. Recovery is user-initiated, not automatic — useless to a sleeping rider.
cases.evidence: snapshot_route_restorer.dart and _onStart null-initialData snapshot path (trackingservice.dart:2023) exist and can restore route state, but they only execute on app relaunch/foreground (onForeground: _onStart, trackingservice.dart:221). Nothing re-evaluates the alarm during the suspended window; restoration is reactive to the user opening the app.

cases.scenario: iOS-specific notification permission handling: the app relies on the plugin's default Darwin prompt and its explicit permission flow skips iOS entirely.
cases.failure_mode: If the user dismisses/denies the iOS notification prompt (or it's never surfaced at the right time), even the one delivery mechanism that could work in-foreground is gone, and the app has no iOS-specific check or re-request to recover — compounding the background-execution gap with a delivery gap.
cases.evidence: permission_service.dart:74-75 _requestNotificationPermission() returns true immediately for non-Android ('Not needed on iOS in the same way'), so there is no explicit iOS notification-permission verification; it relies solely on DarwinInitializationSettings() (notification_service.dart:563) default prompt with no follow-up status check or settings-redirect on denial.

dimension: fail-safe/redundancy/dead-man's-switch (no independent OS-scheduled backstop alarm at ETA clock-time)

cases.scenario: OEM battery killer (Xiaomi MIUI, Realme, Oppo, Vivo, Samsung) silently kills the whole flutter_background_service while rider sleeps mid-route. These skins are the dominant install base in India.
cases.failure_mode: The background isolate is destroyed. All position callbacks stop, alarm evaluation stops, and the alarm never fires. Rider blows past the target stop with zero notification. Product death.
cases.evidence: AndroidManifest.xml declares the service (line 53-54) with no restart guarantee; trackingservice.dart:212 sets autoStart:false and there is NO android_alarm_manager_plus/workmanager/zonedSchedule anywhere in lib/android (repo-wide grep empty). Nothing independent of the isolate is armed for the arrival time, so when the OS reaps the isolate there is no plan B.

cases.scenario: Phone reboots mid-journey (forced OTA update, thermal shutdown, battery dip, kernel panic) while rider sleeps on a long ride.
cases.failure_mode: After reboot the background service never comes back, so the snapshot-based recovery flow is never even reached. Rider sleeps through the stop.
cases.evidence: Manifest has no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission and no boot BroadcastReceiver; trackingservice.dart:212/220 both set autoStart:false. The recovery path at trackingservice.dart:2020-2078 (_onStart with null initialData) can only run if something restarts the isolate — after a reboot nothing does. No OS AlarmClock/zonedSchedule survives the reboot to wake the rider.

cases.scenario: iOS: rider is asleep, screen off, phone stationary on the seat. iOS suspends then terminates the app to reclaim resources (standard iOS background policy for a motionless, backgrounded app).
cases.failure_mode: The Dart isolate is suspended/killed; no position processing, no alarm. iOS gives no location callbacks to a suspended app parked in a tunnel or sitting still between stops.
cases.evidence: onIosBackground (trackingservice.dart:604-607) just calls ensureInitialized() and returns true — no BGTaskScheduler/BGAppRefresh registration, and no scheduled UNTimeIntervalNotification/zonedSchedule armed for ETA (repo grep for BGTaskScheduler/zonedSchedule empty). Once iOS suspends the app there is nothing scheduled at the OS level to wake the rider.

cases.scenario: Rider swipes the app away from recents (thinking they are just tidying the screen before sleeping), then Doze or memory pressure later kills the surviving background isolate.
cases.failure_mode: HeartbeatMonitor detects the foreground death and shows a low-key 'Tracking paused' notification, then STOPS monitoring. If the isolate is subsequently killed, the paused notification is stale and no alarm ever fires. Even in the best case the rider only gets a silent passive notification, not a wake-up.
cases.evidence: HeartbeatMonitor (heartbeat_monitor.dart:45-98) runs inside the background isolate and only watches the FOREGROUND heartbeat; on timeout it calls showTrackingPaused then stop() (line 91). showTrackingPaused (notification_service.dart:1123) issues an ordinary _notificationsPlugin.show — not the full-screen alarm intent — so a sleeping rider will neither hear nor see it, and there is no scheduled fallback if the isolate then dies.

cases.scenario: Low-RAM budget phone (2-3 GB, extremely common in India) under memory pressure: Android LowMemoryKiller reaps the tracking service to free RAM for a foregrounded app the rider opened before dozing off.
cases.failure_mode: Service killed by LMK exactly like the OEM-killer case; no restart is guaranteed for a foreground service under LMK, and no independent alarm is scheduled, so the rider misses the stop.
cases.evidence: Same structural gap: single isolate (trackingservice.dart _onStart), no zonedSchedule/AlarmManager backstop, autoStart:false. The in-isolate HeartbeatMonitor cannot help because it dies with the isolate it lives in (heartbeat_monitor.dart:14, constructed at trackingservice.dart:625 in background-isolate scope).

cases.scenario: Storage-full device: snapshot persistence fails (SharedPreferences refuses the write or the directions payload is too large), then the isolate is later killed and the OS happens to restart it.
cases.failure_mode: Recovery loads a null/stale snapshot and cannot restore the route, so tracking is silently dead even though a restart occurred — and there is still no scheduled fallback alarm to cover the gap.
cases.evidence: saveSnapshot (tracking_state_store.dart:339-390) logs 'SharedPreferences refused snapshot write' and rethrows on payload-too-large; loadSnapshot (tracking_state_store.dart:391-403) returns null on missing/corrupt data, and the recovery branch (trackingservice.dart:2029-2030) simply does nothing when snapshot==null. No ETA-time OS alarm exists to backstop the lost snapshot.

cases.scenario: An uncaught exception in the background isolate (EKF pipeline, reroute decision, or ETA math throws on unexpected real-world input) crashes the isolate mid-ride.
cases.failure_mode: The isolate terminates; because the watchdog (HeartbeatMonitor) is itself inside that isolate, nothing external observes the death and no alarm fires.
cases.evidence: _onStart wires reroute handling that awaits _handleRerouteDecision (trackingservice.dart:1806-1810) and other listeners without an isolate-level supervisor; there is no external process/AlarmManager job monitoring liveness. The only monitor (heartbeat_monitor.dart) shares the isolate's fate, and no independent scheduled notification exists as a last resort.

cases.scenario: Notifications for the app are muted or the POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission is later revoked/never granted, so even a perfectly-alive isolate's show() call is silently dropped by the OS.
cases.failure_mode: The live alarm notification is suppressed by the system and the rider is never woken; there is no alternative loud channel (e.g., a pre-scheduled full-screen-intent alarm) armed as redundancy.
cases.evidence: Every alarm surface routes through _notificationsPlugin.show (notification_service.dart:818/906/968/1100/1202). USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is declared in the manifest but only used on the live in-isolate path; nothing pre-schedules a full-screen alarm via zonedSchedule/AlarmClock as an independent redundant channel, so a single muted/denied notification permission is an unrecoverable single point of failure.

cases.scenario: A Deaf rider naps with the phone resting flat on the padded metro seat or on their lap (not in a pocket against the body). At the target stop the alarm fires: audio is useless to them, so vibration is their only channel.
cases.failure_mode: The single fixed waveform is absorbed by the soft surface and never reaches the body; the rider feels nothing and sleeps past the stop — product death for this population.
cases.evidence: lib/services/alarm_haptics.dart uses ONE hardcoded pattern (const [0,500,250,500,250,1000,500], repeat:0) with no amplitude/escalation and no alternate cue; if Vibration.hasVibrator()!=true it silently `return`s (lines 40-44). notification_service.dart _alarmVibrationPattern is the same fixed 3s loop. grep for torch/flashlight/Wearable/flutter_tts across lib/ and android/ returns nothing — there is no flash, LED, wearable, or escalation fallback whatsoever.

cases.scenario: A hard-of-hearing rider wears Bluetooth hearing aids / BT earbuds and relies on them to hear anything. They arm the alarm and doze; audio is their primary channel.
cases.failure_mode: AlarmPlayer forces the Android ALARM usage stream, which on most OEMs is pinned to the phone's built-in loudspeaker and is NOT routed to the paired hearing-aid/BT media sink. The rider's aids stay silent; with vibration also unreliable (see seat scenario) they perceive no cue.
cases.evidence: lib/services/alarm_player.dart _alarmAudioContext hardcodes AudioContextAndroid(usageType: AndroidUsageType.alarm, audioFocus: gainTransient) and always setVolume(1.0); there is no companion-device / hearing-aid routing option and no user control over output route. The comment at lines 29-34 confirms the deliberate force-to-alarm-stream choice, made only for the media-volume-zero case, with no consideration of BT-routed hearing aids.

cases.scenario: A low-vision rider has set the OS system font size to Large / 200% (extremely common on cheap India-first phones used by elderly). They open the home screen to arm the alarm.
cases.failure_mode: The arming layout is built from fixed fractions of screen size while text scales with the OS setting, so labels, the 'Alert me N stops prior' box, the slider label, and the 'Wake Me!' button overflow/clip or collide; the rider cannot read the current threshold or reliably arm the alarm.
cases.evidence: lib/screens/homescreen.dart sizes containers with SizedBox(height: screenHeight*0.3) for the map and fixed screenHeight/screenWidth fractions for padding, while text uses TextStyle(fontSize: screenWidth*0.045 / *0.05); maptracking.dart uses const TextStyle(fontSize:16/26). grep shows NO textScaler/textScaleFactor/MediaQuery override or clamp anywhere in lib/, so nothing guards against overflow at large scale and there is no large-text/simplified mode.

cases.scenario: A blind TalkBack (or VoiceOver) user swipes through the home screen to set how many stops before their destination to be woken.
cases.failure_mode: The stop/distance/time threshold control is a bare GestureDetector wrapping a Container+Text, so the screen reader announces only the static text 'Alert me 2 stops prior' with no button role and no hint it is actionable. The user cannot discover that tapping opens the value dialog, and cannot change the threshold — they either accept a wrong default or abandon arming.
cases.evidence: lib/screens/homescreen.dart lines 1190-1245: GestureDetector(onTap: showDialog...) -> Container -> Text with no Semantics/button wrapper. grep -c Semantics on homescreen.dart returns 0; zero semanticLabel usage exists in all of lib/.

cases.scenario: A blind rider needs to know WHICH stop to get off at when woken (they cannot glance at the map). The alarm fires in a tunnel near the target station.
cases.failure_mode: The wake cue carries no spoken stop-name. The notification title/body are generic ('Time to Wake Up!' / 'Approaching destination') and there is no TTS announcement of the actual station, so even a rider who hears the alarm has no accessible way to learn which stop is next or confirm it's theirs — they may exit at the wrong station or panic.
cases.evidence: lib/services/notification_service.dart showWakeUpAlarm takes only title/body strings; ensureAlarmNotificationVisible defaults to 'Time to Wake Up!'/'Approaching destination' (lines 858-860). No flutter_tts/TextToSpeech dependency exists (absent from pubspec.yaml and grep of lib/); the full-screen takeover in maptracking.dart is plain Text with no spoken equivalent.

cases.scenario: An elderly / cognitively-impaired first-time rider arms the alarm and wants to confirm it actually works before trusting it enough to fall asleep on a long ride.
cases.failure_mode: There is no 'test/preview alarm' that plays the real wake cue (sound + vibration + full-screen). The ringtone screen previews audio only, so a Deaf/HoH user gets no vibration preview and no one can validate the end-to-end cue. The rider either won't sleep (product fails to deliver its core value) or sleeps on a silently-misconfigured or imperceptible alarm.
cases.evidence: grep for test/preview alarm across lib/ returns nothing. lib/screens/ringtones_screen.dart _togglePreview() only calls _audioPlayer.play() — audio-only preview, no vibration preview, no full end-to-end wake-cue test.

cases.scenario: A TalkBack user toggles between 'stops/distance' and 'time' alarm modes using the mode switch on the home screen while arming.
cases.failure_mode: The Switch has no semantic label saying what it controls; the reader announces only 'switch, on/off' between two loose Text labels ('Time' … 'Stops'/'Distance'), so the user cannot tell which position means which mode and can silently arm the wrong mode — e.g. '2' interpreted as 2 minutes instead of 2 stops — changing when the alarm fires.
cases.evidence: lib/screens/homescreen.dart lines 1177-1188: Row([Text('Time'), Switch(value:_useDistanceMode...), Text(_metroMode?'Stops':'Distance')]) with no Semantics label or grouping; the switch value drives alarmValue/alarmMode computed at lines 630-641.

cases.scenario: An elderly or low-vision rider tries to delete a wrong entry from their recent-destinations autocomplete list, or a motor-impaired rider tries to tap it.
cases.failure_mode: The delete affordance is a ~24px circular GestureDetector (icon 16 + padding 4) — below the 48dp minimum touch target — with no semantic label, so it is invisible to TalkBack and easy to mis-tap for anyone with reduced vision or dexterity; they cannot manage their saved locations and may repeatedly re-select a wrong destination.
cases.evidence: lib/screens/homescreen.dart lines 1126-1145: trailing GestureDetector(onTap:_removeRecentLocation) -> Container(padding: EdgeInsets.all(4)) with Icon(size:16), no Semantics/tooltip, no InkWell/IconButton min-target sizing.

cases.scenario: A low-vision rider (not fully blind, no screen reader) reads the arming screen and the fired-alarm screen in bright daylight on a cheap phone with a dim/low-quality display.
cases.failure_mode: Core text relies on low-contrast greys (white70/black54 hints, grey[200]-on-grey containers, grey.shade600-on-grey.shade300 disabled states) that fall below WCAG AA contrast, so the destination field hint, threshold text, and disabled 'Stop Alarm' state are hard to perceive; the rider may misread or fail to notice the control state.
cases.evidence: lib/screens/homescreen.dart hintStyle Colors.white70/black54 (1099-1101), stepper container grey[200]/grey[700] (1228); maptracking.dart disabledBackgroundColor Colors.grey.shade300 / disabledForegroundColor grey.shade600 (1154-1157). No high-contrast mode and no MediaQuery.highContrast handling anywhere in lib/.

dimension: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mistimed wake — the human and legal consequences (stranding, wrong-place alighting, disorientation, safety incidents) of a silent miss or a spuriously-confident wrong-place alarm, plus the absence of any disclaimer, reliability caveat, or safety framing anywhere in the product.

cases.scenario: The app makes an implicit 'we will wake you' reliability promise with zero legal or safety caveat anywhere. A rider treats WakePoint as their sole alarm for an overnight/late-night ride, it fails (any cause below), and they are stranded — then look for who is responsible.
cases.failure_mode: No disclaimer, no Terms of Service/consent, no 'do not rely on this as your only alarm', no reliability caveat, and no in-app safety framing exist. A harmed rider (stranded alone at a terminus late at night, safety incident) has an unqualified reliability promise to point at, creating direct liability exposure; nothing ever told them to set a backup.
cases.evidence: Full grep of lib/ for disclaimer|liabilit|not rely|backup alarm|do not rely|terms of|consent returns ZERO user-facing hits (only a code comment in lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:47 'It does not rely on events lists' and reliability comments about notifications). User-facing copy is purely confident: 'Time to Wake Up!' (lib/services/notification_service.dart:858), 'Arriving at Destination' (lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:90,112). Permission rationale even over-promises: 'we need to send you a notification to wake you up!' (lib/services/permission_service.dart:83).

cases.scenario: Cheap Indian phone (Xiaomi/MIUI, Realme/Oppo/ColorOS, Vivo/FuntouchOS) with aggressive battery management. Rider starts tracking, pockets the phone, and sleeps. The OS kills the idle foreground service well before the target stop.
cases.failure_mode: Foreground service is silently killed by OEM battery optimization; tracking dies, no alarm ever fires, rider sleeps past the stop and is stranded. The app never requests a battery-optimization exemption, never requests autostart, and shows no OEM-specific guidance — the single largest reliability killer on the India-first target hardware is entirely unmitigated.
cases.evidence: grep of lib/ for ignoreBatteryOpt|batteryOptim|autostart|autoStart|Xiaomi|MIUI|OEM|manufacturer finds nothing except an audio-attribute comment in lib/services/alarm_player.dart:80. Permission flow (lib/services/permission_service.dart requestEssentialPermissions) requests only location, notification, activityRecognition — no REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, no autostart deep-link. Service is autoStart:false (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:212,220) with no keep-alive re-arm.

cases.scenario: Rider sleeps and their intended-stop alarm fails to wake them (dismissed while groggy, DND, or a late GPS fix). The train continues along the SAME correct line to the terminus and then into a depot siding — an unfamiliar, unsafe place late at night.
cases.failure_mode: Riding to the end of the correct line is ON-route, not a deviation, so the termination safety net never engages; and even if it did, it only runs during a reroute/deviation check. There is no 'you have reached the end of the line / final station' backstop alarm independent of the target-stop alarm. The rider is carried into a terminus/depot with no second wake, the worst-case stranding scenario.
cases.evidence: TrackingTerminationPolicy.shouldTerminate only fires on deviation from route (RULE 1/2/3 all require deviationDistanceKm from route, lib/services/tracking_termination_policy.dart:151-217) and is only invoked inside the reroute/deviation path (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:1348-1364). AlarmEventType has finalStation defined (lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:12) but no evaluator branch fires an unconditional end-of-line safety wake; alarms are strictly one-per-leg keyed to the target (RULE 1, alarm_evaluator.dart:159).

cases.scenario: Tunnel section (e.g. Bangalore Metro underground stretch) where the target stop is inside or immediately after the tunnel. GPS drops for the tunnel duration.
cases.failure_mode: The EKF dead-reckoning that is supposed to carry progress through tunnels is built but NOT wired into the production alarm path, so progressMeters stalls at the last pre-tunnel GPS fix. The stops-before / distance-before threshold is never crossed until GPS returns — by which point the train is past the stop. This is the exact 'silent miss' the product's core value prop claims to solve, and it silently does not exist in production.
cases.evidence: grep for ekf_orchestrator|EkfOrchestrator|EkfPipeline|degraded_mode|deadReckon across lib/services and lib/screens finds NO reference in the tracking/alarm path (only lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart exists in isolation). Production alarm evaluation (lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart) is driven purely by progressMeters from GPS; EKF modules in lib/core/ekf/ are validated only in simulation calibrated to one Bangalore ride, per project brief.

cases.scenario: Degraded route context: route metadata/transitLegs is empty or lost (cold restart mid-journey, cache miss, or a fixture-like partial route), while the rider is somewhere along the corridor.
cases.failure_mode: The evaluator's fallback path fires a confident 'Arriving at Destination' alarm on a bare geometric rule (<200m OR 40% into the final leg) with no leg/topology validation. A groggy rider is actively directed to alight, potentially at the wrong place, with the same authoritative wording used for a genuine, validated arrival — a spuriously-confident wrong-place wake.
cases.evidence: lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:73-118 — when transitLegs.isEmpty it fires eventType finalDestination message 'Arriving at Destination' via 'Direct Fire: destination < 200m' (line 86-92) or 'Destination (60% remaining rule)' at progressMeters >= start + 40% (line 106-114), with no branch/parallel-track verification and identical copy to the validated path.

cases.scenario: Groggy rider is woken by the alarm one or two stops early, silences the looping sound, and falls back asleep before their actual stop.
cases.failure_mode: The strict one-alarm-per-leg rule marks the leg fired and suppresses every subsequent evaluation for that leg, so there is NO second/escalating wake before the stop and no snooze-then-re-alarm. A single missed acknowledgment converts into a full missed stop — a very common failure mode for a genuinely sleepy user, with no safety re-arm.
cases.evidence: lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:159-168 — RULE 1 returns null once firedLegIds contains the leg id ('Leg already fired, skipping'). No snooze/re-arm/escalation logic exists (grep for snooze|rearm|re-arm in trackingservice/alarm_evaluator finds none). Alarm persistence is only ongoing:true/loop for the FIRST firing (notification_service.dart:733-734), not a re-trigger after user dismissal.

cases.scenario: Rider grants notifications at start, then the phone enters night-time Do Not Disturb / silent, or the rider revokes notification permission after tracking has begun.
cases.failure_mode: Permission and DND state are validated only once at journey start; there is no runtime re-check or 'you are no longer protected' warning. If the wake-up channel is suppressed by a scheduled DND profile the rider may not be woken. Mitigations exist (alarm audio usage + category=alarm + fullScreenIntent) but there is no explicit channel DND-bypass flag and no runtime verification, so the outcome is device/OEM-dependent rather than guaranteed.
cases.evidence: Permissions checked once at start only (lib/screens/homescreen.dart:482-483, gate at 491); no re-check during tracking. Mitigations: lib/services/alarm_player.dart:13-24 sets AndroidUsageType.alarm, and lib/services/notification_service.dart:726-731 sets Importance.max, category alarm, fullScreenIntent:true — but grep for setBypassDnd|bypassDnd returns no explicit channel DND-bypass, and no runtime DND/permission monitor exists.

cases.scenario: Deviation-triggered termination fires while the rider is asleep — e.g. carried well past the route and stopped 5km+ away. The app wakes them with the termination notification.
cases.failure_mode: The rider is woken in an unfamiliar and possibly unsafe location by a bare status message ('Tracking ended: You appear to have stopped X km from your route') that offers no orientation, no 'you may have missed your stop — check your surroundings / next return service' guidance, and no safety framing for a disoriented late-night rider. The wake is technically delivered but human-unsafe, and it doubles as the moment the product silently gives up.
cases.evidence: lib/services/trackingservice.dart:1476-1494 shows title 'Tracking Ended' with body = raw termination userMessage; those messages (lib/services/tracking_termination_policy.dart:157-159, 172-174, 208-210) are diagnostic ('You appear to have stopped Xkm from your route' / 'heading away from your destination') with no actionable safety guidance, and allowContinueTracking:false ends tracking outright.

scenario: Metro rider asleep; train enters a long tunnel with full GPS blackout and reaches the target stop while still underground before GPS returns. Claimed failure: no new Position events arrive, so the alarm is never re-evaluated and fires only after GPS returns past the stop (product death).
evidence: Alarm evaluation in production has exactly ONE trigger path, and it is edge-driven by real Position events. Chain: LocationManager.positionStream -> LocationStreamHandler._handlePositionUpdate (location_stream_handler.dart:209-213, 220-273) -> onCheckAlarm (wired at trackingservice.dart:2169-2173) -> _checkAndTriggerAlarm (trackingservice.dart:1213) -> AlarmController.checkAndTriggerAlarm (trackingservice.dart:1291). The only other caller of _checkAndTriggerAlarm is checkAlarmForTest, marked @visibleForTesting (trackingservice.dart:2436-2441). LocationManager.positionStream is fed only by real GPS (_onRealPosition) or simulation/injected positions (location_manager.dart:95,106,160,280); Geolocator emits nothing during a blackout, so no synthetic ticks occur. The EKF does NOT rescue this: onEkfUpdate merely stores _lastEkfState = state (trackingservice.dart:2165-2167), and _lastEkfState is consumed ONLY inside _resolveAlarmRouteState/_checkAndTriggerAlarm (trackingservice.dart:1176-1184), which is never invoked without a Position event. SensorFusionManager's own fused-position controller (sensor_fusion.dart:220) has no subscriber that re-injects into the alarm path. The periodic timers do not re-evaluate: _gpsCheckTimer/_handleGpsCheckTick only start fusion, re-post notifications, broadcast state, and set time-alarm eligibility (location_stream_handler.dart:418-452) with no onCheckAlarm call; HeartbeatMonitor only detects foreground death (heartbeat_monitor.dart:45); AlarmController._alarmStopPollTimer polls for user stop AFTER firing (alarm_controller.dart:1301-1400). Therefore, with GPS silent, evaluation is frozen until the first post-tunnel Position event — after the stop. This matches the stated fact that the EKF is built but not wired into production alarm logic.
fix_direction: Add a clock-driven evaluation tick during GPS dropout: from onEkfUpdate (or _gpsCheckTimer when silentFor >= gpsDropoutBuffer), synthesize a Position from the latest dead-reckoned EKF state (s/lat/lng) and call onCheckAlarm/_checkAndTriggerAlarm, so the alarm re-evaluates against EKF route progress while underground instead of only on real GPS events.

scenario: Very noisy cheap accelerometer (poor MEMS part) during a GPS dropout / tunnel segment: the sensor's stationary noise floor exceeds the fixed variance gates, so static-bias estimation and ZUPT never trigger, bias is never removed, 1-D DR position drifts unbounded, and station snaps are rejected.
evidence:
Every IMU-quality gate is a hard-coded absolute constant with no per-device noise-floor calibration or adaptive scaling (grep for noise-floor/adaptive/calibration in lib/core/ekf and lib/services returns nothing but the unrelated sigmaS margin). A cheap MEMS whose stationary accel-variance floor is > ~0.5 m^2/s^4 defeats the entire chain:

1. Static bias init is gated at accelVar<0.5 && gyroVar<0.1 (ekf_orchestrator.dart:713). If never satisfied, _biasInitialized stays false and _estimatedInitialBias stays null, so the DR path at ekf_orchestrator.dart:748-750 returns raw aFwd with NO bias subtraction -> the constant bias integrates into unbounded position drift.

2. All three ZUPT paths die (zupt_detector.dart:51,58,71-75): imuQuiet needs accelVar<1.0 (line 8/51), imuUltraQuiet needs accelVar<0.15 && gyroVar<0.05 (line 58), and every path also needs either velocityLow (which is drifting garbage during DR) or motionHint. 

3. motionHint is never true because the motion classifier's stationary test is accelVar<0.5 && gyroVar<0.10 (motion_classifier.dart:135-136), which a noisy part never meets -> never MotionState.stationary.

4. Station association hard-requires zuptConfirmed as a precondition (station_association.dart:135, early-return 199) -> permanent ZUPT_NOT_CONFIRMED, so DR position is never snapped/corrected. Numeric clamps (velocity +/-25 m/s ekf_pipeline.dart:211, sigmaS cap) only prevent NaN; they do NOT bound meaningful drift (25 m/s of wrong-direction drift is catastrophic for a wake alarm). DegradedMode (degraded_mode.dart) only flips a boolean on high sigma / ZUPT gap; it has no conservative fail-safe alarm. The failure mode is exactly as claimed. Note this is currently latent because the EKF is not yet wired into production alarm logic, but the DR subsystem itself is genuinely broken for high-noise sensors.
fix_direction: Replace the fixed absolute variance gates with a per-device stationary noise-floor estimated at session start (e.g. baseline accel/gyro variance while the phone is known-still), then set ZUPT / bias-init / motion-classifier thresholds as a multiple of that measured floor (adaptive) instead of hard-coded 0.5/0.15/0.05; alternatively gate ZUPT on a relative-quiet detector (variance below k*rolling-baseline) so a noisy MEMS can still register a stop.

scenario: Device master Location Services toggled OFF at OS level while app location permission stays granted — at journey start, or mid-journey. Claim: start shows a recoverable error dialog; mid-journey the position stream silently stops with no user-facing warning, so no alarm fires and the rider is never told tracking is dead.
evidence:
START (handled): homescreen.dart:920-926 `_getCurrentLocation()` wraps `Geolocator.getCurrentPosition()` in try/catch returning null; the tracking-start path at homescreen.dart:538-548 checks null and shows a recoverable dialog "Could not get your current location. Please enable location services." then aborts start. So the start half matches the claim and is covered (though it never opens location settings and doesn't distinguish service-off from other failures).

MID-JOURNEY (genuine open gap — confirmed): The production GPS stream has NO service-status monitoring and swallows the disable signal:
- location_manager.dart:95-100 `_startRealGps()` subscribes to `Geolocator.getPositionStream(...)` with `onError: (e) => _log.severe(...)`. When OS location is turned off, geolocator terminates/errors the stream (LocationServiceDisabledException); this handler only logs it, does NOT forward an error to `_positionController`, does NOT re-check service state, and does NOT attempt restart. The broadcast `positionStream` simply goes silent.
- location_stream_handler.dart:209-213 (the production background alarm path) does `LocationManager().positionStream.listen(...)` with NO onError at all, so downstream never learns tracking died.
- The only silence-detector, `_checkGpsDropout` (location_stream_handler.dart:521-531), treats the silence identically to a tunnel and just spins up sensor fusion / EKF dead-reckoning. But per project state the EKF is not wired into alarm logic: `onEkfUpdate` only stores `_lastEkfState` for snapshots (lines 585-590, 402-404), and `onCheckAlarm` is invoked ONLY inside `_handlePositionUpdate` when a real Position arrives (line 268-273). The periodic `_handleGpsCheckTick` (428-452) never calls onCheckAlarm. So with GPS silent, zero alarm evaluation runs.
- grep over lib/ confirms `getServiceStatusStream()` and `isLocationServiceEnabled()` exist ONLY in test/process_death_recovery_test.dart's MockGeolocatorPlatform, never in production. No watchdog escalates prolonged GPS silence to a user-facing warning.
Net mid-journey outcome: tracking dies silently, EKF (unwired) never fires, no alarm, no notification that tracking is dead — the fire-late = product-death case.
fix_direction: In LocationManager (or the background tracking start), subscribe to `Geolocator.getServiceStatusStream()` and add a "GPS silent longer than N seconds" watchdog escalation: on service-disabled or prolonged silence, raise a high-priority user-facing notification telling the rider tracking has stopped and location must be re-enabled — rather than silently entering dead-reckoning that never fires an alarm. Also forward the geolocator onError downstream instead of only logging it.

scenario: WRONG DIRECTION: rider boards the correct metro line at the wrong platform and travels away from the destination, underground (no GPS). EKF arc-length 's' is used as alarm progress with no signed direction-along-route check, so the app "advances" toward the modeled destination and fires a spurious arrival alarm while the true stop is never reached.
evidence:
Every link in the claimed failure chain is present in production code, and no guard catches it:

1) Deviation/soft-lock IS skipped on metro legs. lib/services/trackingservice.dart:1120-1122 comment: "Metro legs use 'Ground Truth' GPS speed logic and effectively ignore position deviation (tunnels)." The entire soft-lock block is gated by `if (!isMetroStep)` at line 1143. So on a metro leg no lateral/position sanity check runs.

2) Metro-leg alarm progress = EKF s. lib/services/trackingservice.dart:1176-1184: when `isMetroStep` (or EKF degraded/metro mode), `progressMeters = ekfState.s`. This EKF value overrides the GPS snap progress.

3) s is a magnitude-integrated, monotonic-forward quantity with NO signed route-direction check. lib/core/ekf/ekf_pipeline.dart:201 `_s = _s + _v * dt + 0.5*aBias*dt2` integrates forward velocity derived from the accelerometer's along-track axis (aFwd), which is positive whenever the train accelerates in its own direction of travel — independent of whether that direction points toward or away from the route destination. Underground there is no GPS (`onGpsFix`/`projectLatLng` at ekf_orchestrator.dart:237,264 never runs) to supply the sign of motion relative to the polyline. Worse, on metro legs reverse is explicitly forbidden: ekf_orchestrator.dart:288 `_pipeline.setAllowReverse(!isMetroLeg)`, and ekf_pipeline.dart:204-208 clamps `if(_v<0)_v=0; if(_s<sOld)_s=sOld;`. ekf_types.dart:8 documents s as "monotonic public". So s can ONLY increase.

4) Increasing s trips the stops-based metro alarm. lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:776-797 counts `passedIntermediate` purely as `progressMeters >= stopMeters` and fires when `remainingStopsToTarget <= thresholdN`. A monotonically rising s therefore "passes" modeled stops and fires an Arriving/Transfer alarm even though the rider is physically receding from the true stop.

5) No wrong-direction/wrong-platform guard exists anywhere. grep for wrong-direction/opposite/reverse-direction/heading-mismatch found nothing applicable. The only "moving away" logic (lib/services/tracking_termination_policy.dart:177-217) is inert here: it early-returns unless a `_deviationState` is already set (line 132), i.e. it requires the rider to be OFF-route laterally — but a wrong-platform rider is ON the correct polyline (lateral offset ~0), so no deviation state is ever created. It is also pure GPS straight-line distance and never runs underground.

The reverse case (elevated/GPS section) is consistent: SnapToRouteEngine projects onto the one-directional polyline, so opposite travel yields non-increasing progress; the stops-based counter at alarm_evaluator.dart:776 never advances and no alarm fires. Either way the rider misses.
fix_direction: On metro legs, add a signed along-route direction gate before letting EKF s advance the alarm: seed/validate travel direction from any available signal at boarding or intermittent GPS (sign of sGps delta, or device heading vs route tangent from route_geometry.tangentAt), and when the confirmed direction is anti-parallel to the route (or GPS progress is decreasing on elevated sections) suppress "advance", raise a wrong-direction/wrong-platform warning, and do NOT fire the arrival alarm.

scenario: Low max sensor sample rate / aggressive IMU batching: power-saving SoCs deliver accelerometer samples in bursts rather than steadily at ~100Hz.
evidence: Production IMU wiring (SensorFusionManager, the only path feeding real sensors into the EKF) timestamps each ImuSample from a Stopwatch read at PROCESSING time, not the true sample time: lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart:224-228 uses _imuClock.elapsedMicroseconds inside the accelerometer listener. It ignores the hardware per-sample timestamp that sensors_plus already provides (AccelerometerEvent.timestamp — sensors_plus_platform_interface-2.0.1/lib/src/accelerometer_event.dart:39). So batched samples processed back-to-back DO get near-identical timestamps → dt≈0, confirming the scenario's mechanism. HOWEVER the specific corruption claims are largely mitigated: (1) velocity integration is NOT corrupted — ekf_pipeline.dart:112-133 guards dt: dt<=0 skip, dt>1s reset velocity/bias, and dt<minDt(0.001) or dt>maxDt(0.2) → inflate covariance and return WITHOUT integrating, so dt≈0 burst samples are dropped, not integrated as garbage; (2) sampleRateHz (ekf_orchestrator.dart:588, (n-1)/duration over a 2.56s trim window) stays roughly correct because the Stopwatch is a real monotonic clock and bursts arrive at real intervals, so window-average rate ≈ true rate; (3) time-based ZUPT/motion gating (zupt_detector.dart:83-88 dwell=800ms; variance window 0.75s) is measured on the same monotonic clock and remains approximately real-time-correct across bursts. The residual OPEN failure: those very guards turn batching into a DR-stall. Under batch report latency > maxDt=0.2s (plausible on aggressive power-save/Doze on cheap phones), every burst-boundary sample hits the marginal-dt branch (ekf_pipeline.dart:127-133) and is skipped — or if >1s, zeroes velocity (line 118-126) — so dead reckoning freezes during the exact GPS dropout it exists to cover. Even under sub-0.2s batching only one boundary sample per burst integrates, over a whole-burst dt with a single stale acceleration, discarding intra-burst dynamics. There is no batch-aware handling and no sensor-interval/batching configuration on the stream (uses default accelerometerEvents at sensor_fusion.dart:184).
fix_direction: Timestamp ImuSample from the hardware sample clock (AccelerometerEvent.timestamp, already exposed by sensors_plus 7.0) instead of the processing-time Stopwatch, so each batched sample integrates with its true ~10ms dt regardless of burst delivery; and when a large boundary dt does occur, sub-step the Kalman predict (split into ~50-100Hz increments) rather than skipping via the maxDt guard, so DR keeps advancing through batched delivery.

scenario: Budget Android phone with no gyroscope enters a metro tunnel; GPS drops and EKF dead-reckoning must carry progress. Claim: gyroscopeEvents never emits so gyro is treated as identically zero, degrading TiltFilter/MotionClassifier and causing ZUPT/station-association gates to rarely pass, so DR drifts and station snaps are rejected.
evidence: Premise TRUE but consequence BACKWARDS. (1) Gyro IS silently zeroed: lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart:229-231 defaults gx/gy/gz to 0.0 when _lastGyro is null (init null at line 179), and the gyro subscription at lines 255-267 swallows errors/absence (handleError plus onError cancel plus cancelOnError true), leaving _lastGyro null forever. Grep for hasGyro/gyroAvailable/isSupported/capability across lib/ returns nothing: no gyroscope-availability detection exists. (2) The claimed failure DIRECTION is wrong. Every gyro-dependent gate has the form gyroVariance less-than threshold: zupt_detector.dart:51 (thresh 0.40) and line 58 (thresh 0.05), motion_classifier.dart:136 (thresh 0.10). With gyroVariance identically 0 these terms are ALWAYS satisfied, so gates pass MORE readily, not rarely. Station association (station_association.dart:106-210) has NO gyroVariance dependency: it gates on isMetroLeg/zuptConfirmed/dwell/candidate-window/sigmaS, so snaps are not rejected because of gyro; easier ZUPT makes them more likely. The real risk is the opposite: false-positive ZUPT/stationary during cruise, partly mitigated by accel-variance gates and the degraded forward-accel override at motion_classifier.dart:127. (3) TiltFilter does not collapse: with zero gyro, _integrateGyro returns orientation unchanged and it falls back to accel-LPF gravity blending (tilt_filter.dart:88-91 and 149-162), an accel-only complementary filter, degraded but functional; its gravitySample substitute path is never fed in production because SensorFusionManager subscribes only to accelerometerEvents and gyroscopeEvents. (4) The entire DR path is behind enableEkf (default false, sensor_fusion.dart:90; enabled only when routeGeometry is non-null at location_stream_handler.dart:573) and per project context not wired into alarm logic yet.
fix_direction: Add explicit gyroscope-availability detection at fusion start; when absent, source orientation from Android's fused gravity/rotation-vector sensor into TiltFilter's already-supported gravitySample path, and mark gyro features invalid so the gyroVariance gates in zupt_detector/motion_classifier are deliberately neutralized (tighten accel-variance and velocity gates to prevent false-positive stationary/ZUPT during cruise) rather than silently reading a constant zero as quiet.

Gate the alarm pipeline on position.accuracy: reject or hold fixes coarser than ~150-200m so they never advance progress or fire an alarm (fall back to EKF/last-good-progress), and at tracking start detect a coarse-only permission grant to warn the user before they sleep.
scenario: Android 12+ Approximate location only grant returns 1-3km-accuracy fixes despite requesting LocationAccuracy.high; distance/stop alarms compute against a fix km off, firing kilometres early or reporting not-yet-near so the alarm fires late or never.
evidence: Alarm pipeline never inspects position.accuracy nor detects coarse-only grant. Flow: location_stream_handler.dart:270 -> trackingservice.dart:1213 _checkAndTriggerAlarm -> _resolveAlarmRouteState:1059 -> SnapToRouteEngine.snap:1088 -> AlarmEvaluator.evaluateCoinciding. SnapToRouteEngine.snap (snap_to_route.dart:43) takes no accuracy arg and full-route-searches when offset>500m (snap_to_route.dart:84), so a 1-3km-off fix snaps to a wrong point -> wrong progressMeters. AlarmEvaluator.evaluateCoinciding (alarm_evaluator.dart:48) fires purely on progressMeters vs stop boundaries with no uncertainty input; metro stops ~1km apart so km error crosses boundaries, firing early or missing. Accuracy-aware code is unwired or unprotective: GpsHealthMonitor accuracy>50m degraded (gps_health_monitor.dart:25,113) has no production caller (only its own file+test); SoftLockManager only WIDENS corridor to 200m when accuracy>20m (soft_lock_manager.dart:39-42), non-metro only, merely logs deviation (trackingservice.dart:1164-1171) without gating alarm progress; eta_engine gpsAccuracyThreshold=30 (line 15,484) only weights ETA blending, never rejects a fix. No coarse-vs-precise detection: permission_service.dart requests location/locationAlways only, never checks precision. EKF inflates R by accuracyMeters (ekf_pipeline.dart:302) but is not wired into production alarm logic.

scenario: Rider clears the app from recents (or another app evicts it) before dozing, trusting the persistent tracking notification. Claim: swiping the UI away stops heartbeats, the service flips to paused, shows "Resume to continue", self-suspends alarm checking, and the wake-up never fires.
evidence: The claimed core mechanism — pausing self-suspends alarm checking — does not exist. HeartbeatMonitor's timeout action (lib/services/tracking/heartbeat_monitor.dart:83-91) only sets the paused flag, swaps notifications, and stops its OWN timer (stop() at 101-105 cancels just _timer); it never stops the location stream, position subscription, or AlarmController. The background isolate owns an independent GPS subscription (startLocationStream(service) in _onStart, trackingservice.dart:1686), so it keeps receiving positions after the UI isolate dies. Crucially, NO alarm-firing code gates on isPaused: the only production reads of isPaused are snapshot_route_restorer.dart:30 (service-start route restore) and trackingservice.dart:1762 (resume handler). Neither location_stream_handler.dart nor alarm_controller.dart reads isPaused in the processing/firing path (grep-confirmed). Therefore, in the exact case described (service alive, paused notification visible), the alarm still fires. Restart also recovers: _onStart sets paused=false (trackingservice.dart:1598) before restoring route + restarting the stream. Residual gaps keeping this PARTIAL rather than fully COVERED: (1) misleading "Resume to continue" notification text implies tracking halted when it hasn't; (2) a concurrency race — setPaused(false) at trackingservice.dart:1598 is not awaited while SnapshotRouteRestorer reads isPaused at 1613 inside a concurrent unawaited block (1610), so on an aggressive-OEM kill-then-restart where paused was already persisted true, restoreFromStoreIfActiveAndNotPaused (snapshot_route_restorer.dart:30-31) can skip rebuilding the route.
fix_direction: Reword the paused notification so it does not imply tracking stopped (tracking genuinely continues in the surviving-service case), and harden the restart path by awaiting setPaused(false) before the restorer runs — or restore the route whenever active==true regardless of paused — so a kill-then-restart while paused==true cannot skip route rebuild.
